facts.text: Brute-force field exposure is intrinsically bad at proving rare-event safety.
facts.quote: Brute-force field exposure is intrinsically bad at proving rare-event safety.

facts.text: RAND's 2016 analysis calculated that demonstrating injury and fatality reliability by naturalistic driving alone would require hundreds of millions of miles and sometimes hundreds of billions of miles.
facts.quote: RAND's 2016 analysis calculated that demonstrating injury and fatality reliability by naturalistic driving alone would take "hundreds of millions of miles and sometimes hundreds of billions of miles".

facts.text: University of Michigan accelerated-evaluation researchers learned naturalistic driving distributions, deliberately generated more critical interactions, and used importance sampling to recover unbiased estimates for the modelled event class.
facts.quote: learned naturalistic driving distributions, deliberately generated far more critical interactions and used importance sampling to recover unbiased estimates for the event class that was modelled

facts.text: University of Michigan accelerated-evaluation researchers reported orders-of-magnitude acceleration in lane-change and car-following cases during 2016 to 2017; the evidence is from on-road vehicles.
facts.quote: reporting orders-of-magnitude acceleration in lane-change and car-following cases (2016 to 2017).

facts.text: Feng et al., in Nature in 2023, trained dense-reinforcement-learning background agents to validate automated vehicles in an accelerated mode without loss of unbiasedness; the evidence is on-road.
facts.quote: Feng et al. (Nature, 2023) trained dense-reinforcement-learning background agents that validate automated vehicles "in an accelerated mode, without loss of unbiasedness".

facts.text: Adaptive stress testing by Corso et al. at Stanford searches for failures in simulation using dynamic programming and scene decomposition; the evidence is on-road.
facts.quote: Adaptive stress testing (Corso et al., Stanford) searches for failures in simulation by dynamic programming and scene decomposition.

facts.text: Liu and Feng's “Curse of rarity,” published in Nature Communications in 2024, explains that safety-critical events are rare and embedded in a very high-dimensional environment, making the distribution tail hard to learn and validate.
facts.quote: Liu and Feng's "Curse of rarity" (Nature Communications, 2024) explains why safety-critical events are both rare and embedded in a very high-dimensional environment, making the tail hard to learn and validate.

facts.text: Acceleration factors from the cited on-road statistical validation research should not be copied into a mining or construction business case.
facts.quote: None of those acceleration factors should be copied into a mining or construction business case.

facts.text: Mine roads, pedestrian behaviour, haul-truck dynamics, berms, loaders, reversing and job-site work rules have different distributions from the on-road acceleration precedents.
facts.quote: Mine roads, pedestrian behaviour, haul-truck dynamics, berms, loaders, reversing and job-site work rules have different distributions

facts.text: The off-road exposure dataset needed to reweight the different mining and construction distributions has not been demonstrated.
facts.quote: the off-road exposure dataset needed to reweight them has not been demonstrated.

facts.text: Stratified sampling forces coverage of weather, site, machine and scenario strata rather than allowing easy, common conditions to dominate testing.
facts.quote: Forces coverage of weather, site, machine and scenario strata instead of letting easy, common conditions dominate

facts.text: Strata used in stratified sampling must represent the real domain.
facts.quote: Strata must represent the real domain

facts.text: Importance or rare-event sampling concentrates simulation and controlled tests near critical boundaries.
facts.quote: Concentrates simulation and controlled tests near critical boundaries [32, 33]

facts.text: Importance or rare-event sampling requires the original probability distribution to be known well enough to reweight correctly.
facts.quote: The original probability distribution must be known well enough to reweight correctly

facts.text: Sequential confidence testing allows a test to stop when predefined evidence thresholds are reached rather than at an arbitrary exposure count.
facts.quote: Lets a test stop when predefined evidence thresholds are reached rather than at an arbitrary exposure count

facts.text: Sequential confidence testing requires the acceptance threshold and statistical test to be fixed in advance.
facts.quote: Acceptance threshold and statistical test fixed in advance

facts.text: Bayesian or hierarchical pooling across variants shares information among genuinely similar machine families while retaining variant uncertainty.
facts.quote: Shares information among genuinely similar machine families while retaining variant uncertainty. **Expert opinion**

facts.text: Bayesian or hierarchical pooling across machine variants requires a justified similarity model; otherwise pooling can hide a bad variant.
facts.quote: The similarity model must be justified, otherwise pooling hides a bad variant

facts.text: Coverage statistics and confidence bounds quantify observed miss and intervention rates and prevent a large amount of driving alone from masquerading as evidence.
facts.quote: Coverage statistics and confidence bounds quantify observed miss and intervention rates and stop "we drove a lot" from masquerading as evidence

facts.text: Coverage statistics and confidence bounds require a clearly defined denominator, representative sampling, event labelling and a statistical test plan written before testing.
facts.quote: they require a clearly defined denominator, representative sampling, event labelling and a statistical test plan written before testing.

facts.text: Absence of failures is not proof of zero risk.
facts.quote: Absence of failures is not proof of zero risk

facts.text: No statistical method compensates for an incorrect exposure model, missing hazard classes, unknown unknowns or an unvalidated simulator.
facts.quote: no statistical method compensates for an incorrect exposure model, missing hazard classes, unknown unknowns or an unvalidated simulator.
